card._standing: The Track 1 -> Track 2 hand-off. Written 2026-09-06 from the research record (H003-H009, methodology 070-074) and public literature; revised to version 3 on 2026-09-18 and to version 4 on 2026-09-19 (step 8, methodology 115-118) from the oracle reply (083) and iteration 2's steps 2-6 (methodology 088, 092, 096, 097, 099, 101, 106, 109). Coordinate-free by rule: it names the gene, the protein and the variant classes, never a position. Revised, never edited: bump `version` and append to `history`.

case._mondo_note: Open Targets resolves MVA1 to MONDO_0009759 (verified live 2026-09-06 through disease_search on the disease name); the earlier MONDO:0009551 was wrong

context_standard_of_care.note: the drugs already given for the tumour context; they can reach a high rung automatically (approved, paediatric trials) and are excluded from the repurposing shortlist because giving them is not a repurposing
context_standard_of_care.source: PMID 41749943 and 40421977 (rhabdomyosarcoma treatment landscape and maintenance regimens)

gene.protein: BubR1 (mitotic checkpoint serine/threonine-protein kinase BUB1 beta)

alleles.label: stop
alleles.reading: null allele: truncates BubR1 upstream of the C-terminal kinase domain

alleles.label: missense
alleles.classification: gnomAD-absent; AlphaMissense likely_pathogenic (log-likelihood-ratio lane 4.33, iteration 2 methodology 099); CADD 24.5
alleles.reading: presumed hypomorph: a partly working copy inside the C-terminal kinase domain (CDD cd14029)
alleles.structure: outside every InterPro entry typed 'domain' (inside the protein-kinase-like superfamily entry), AlphaFold pLDDT 91.06 at the residue - the model is confident about the region (iteration 2, methodology 106, H040 refuted)

mechanism.class: loss-of-function, hypomorphic (compound heterozygote: one null allele + one partly functional allele)
mechanism.status: confirmed: the oracle's reply to submission 1 is a full match at rank 1 for the stop + missense pair (methodology 083, H009 supported), so the trans configuration is the answer key's statement, not an inference
mechanism.pathway: spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC) - mitotic checkpoint complex (MCC) formation and APC/C-CDC20 inhibition
mechanism.immediate_effect: reduced BubR1 abundance and checkpoint signalling; weakened kinetochore-microtubule attachment error correction
downstream: mosaic aneuploidy in dividing tissues (variegated: different chromosomes in different cells)
aneuploidy-associated proteotoxic and metabolic stress in surviving cells
cancer predisposition: rhabdomyosarcoma, Wilms tumour, leukaemia (MVA1 spectrum)
growth restriction (short stature, failure to thrive, IUGR), nephrocalcinosis
mechanism.complete_loss: embryonic lethal in mouse and human - full inhibition of BubR1 is not a therapeutic direction

literature.role: Hanks 2004: biallelic BUB1B mutations cause MVA with cancer predisposition; truncating + missense genotypes
Suijkerbuijk 2010: MVA patient cells have strongly reduced BUBR1 and a weakened SAC; missense alleles act as hypomorphs
BubR1 insufficiency, aneuploidy and premature ageing in the mouse hypomorph

repurposing_directions.name: SAC reinforcement / chromosomal-instability reduction
repurposing_directions.rationale: compensate for reduced BubR1 signalling; agents that prolong mitotic checkpoint arrest or stabilise kinetochore-microtubule attachments

repurposing_directions.name: aneuploidy-selective stress exploitation
repurposing_directions.rationale: aneuploid cells carry proteotoxic and energy stress; published aneuploidy-selective killing (AICAR-class energy stress, chloroquine-class autophagy stress, HSP90/HSF1 axis); human aneuploid cells depend on increased RNA and protein degradation (proteasome, autophagy - PMID 39247952) and mount a TFEB-driven lysosomal stress response (PMID 26404941). Caveat: this direction kills aneuploid cells - it is a tumour-context and chemoprevention angle, not a treatment of the constitutional mosaic state

repurposing_directions.name: proteostasis / BubR1 stabilisation for a hypomorph
repurposing_directions.rationale: a partly working protein can be stabilised or its turnover slowed; explore APC/C, deacetylase and chaperone routes; note BubR1 acetylation regulates its stability; SIRT2 deacetylates BubR1 (K668) and NAD+ repletion with nicotinamide mononucleotide raised BubR1 abundance in vivo and extended lifespan in BubR1-hypomorphic mice (PMID 24825348); BubR1 overexpression protects against aneuploidy and cancer (PMID 23242215); HDAC2/3 deacetylation of BubR1 silences the checkpoint (PMID 28985013)

repurposing_directions.name: cancer prevention in the MVA1 tumour context
repurposing_directions.rationale: the child's presenting tumour is rhabdomyosarcoma; approved agents with a chemoprevention or surveillance rationale in aneuploidy-driven tumours; de novo cholesterol synthesis is a non-redundant vulnerability of rhabdomyosarcoma cells (PMID 41249736)

constraints.eligibility: market-approved drugs only (challenge rules, Track 2 definition); ChEMBL max_phase 4 or an FDA label is the evidence of approval

not_used.DrugBank: licence required for programmatic access; name-dropped by the form but not queried

history.change: first card, from the iteration-1 record
correct the MONDO id after the first snapshot resolved the disease by name

trans confirmed (083); measured facts F1-F9 from iteration 2 steps 2-6 (dosage, copy number, structure, pathogenicity lanes, P(trans), phase; aneuploidy burden marked unmeasured); D2 gains proteasome and TFEB seeds, D3 the SIRT2/CBP acetylation axis, D4 HMGCR; anti-directions and the evidence ladder added; anti-directions carry a mechanism-of-action pattern; the tumour context names its standard-of-care drugs so the shortlist can exclude them; D4 marked as the tumour-context direction so the trial-based rungs apply to it alone (113)

F8 measured by step 8: no autosome above its 2-3 % detection limit in the sequenced sample (methodology 115-118, H051-H053, H055-H057 supported; H054 open); D2's standing restated as literature-only. No rung, seed, direction or anti-direction changed (H061)

measured_facts.value: confirmed by the oracle (full match at rank 1, 100 rank points, F-max 1.0)
measured_facts.implication: the mechanism argument rests on a confirmed compound heterozygote; the card's biggest rigor caveat is closed

measured_facts.value: both lead alleles at one-copy multiplicity in the raw reads, posterior 1.0, read without an aligner or a caller
measured_facts.implication: a null + hypomorph genotype, not null + null: some BubR1 is made, so stabilising it (D3) is a live direction

measured_facts.value: every target-gene exon region at two copies (median 2.00 autosomal, null band [1.028, 2.823]); no exon deletion in the gene
measured_facts.implication: no hidden third allele or deletion; the two alleles are the whole genotype

measured_facts.value: 164 credible consensus structural variants genome-wide, none in the gene; 6,823 phase blocks, none reaching the gene's coding span - phase is unmeasured in the reads
measured_facts.implication: trans is the oracle's statement (F1), not a read measurement; the report says so

measured_facts.value: outside every InterPro domain-typed entry, at 95.4 % along the protein, in a region AlphaFold models at pLDDT 91.06
measured_facts.implication: 'hypomorph' rests on the allele class, the MVA1 literature and the pathogenicity predictors, not on a curated catalytic-site hit; the catalytic-dead versus unstable-protein question stays open and D3 is argued as a dosage direction, not a folding one

measured_facts.value: AlphaMissense likely_pathogenic, log-likelihood-ratio contribution 4.33 (capped at moderate); the pair leads 51,920 biallelic hypotheses over 11,465 genes with no hard filter
measured_facts.implication: quantifies 'damaging' for the partly working copy

measured_facts.value: undetermined - 5 of 50 leading alleles reach gnomAD v2 at all
measured_facts.implication: population phasing cannot corroborate F1; F1 stands alone

measured_facts.fact: aneuploidy burden in the sequenced sample
measured_facts.value: MEASURED (iteration 2, step 8): no autosome carries a mosaic whole-chromosome or whole-arm aneuploidy above its own detection limit - 2 % of cells on chr1-6 and 3 % on chr7-22 at 80 % power (fold-over B-allele deviation, over-dispersion 0.0162 measured, 127,913 heterozygous-call rows); X and Y cannot be read by allele balance in a male and the dosage route (H054) has not run; sub-arm events were never testable. The statistic iteration 1 used (037) had no power at any fraction tested
measured_facts.implication: the sequenced sample shows no aneuploid population that a drug could be aimed at; the tissue is not named by the delivery and a karyotype's fraction is measured in cultured cells, so this is not a statement about the diagnosis. Direction D2 (aneuploidy-selective stress) therefore stays a tumour-context and chemoprevention angle argued from the literature; it cannot be argued from a measured burden in this child, and the report ranks it below D3 and D4 for that reason

measured_facts.value: the knowledge route placed the gene at rank 293 of 815 and its own top two genes were decoys; the fused blind ranking still put the confirmed pair first
measured_facts.implication: the drug literature is searched per drug and per direction, never trusted as a ranker on its own

anti_directions.name: further checkpoint weakening
anti_directions.agents: Mps1/TTK inhibitors, Aurora B inhibitors, MAD2/BUB1 inhibition - none market-approved
anti_directions.why: aneuploid cancer cells are selectively killed by mitotic checkpoint inhibition (PMID 33505028) - the same logic makes a constitutionally SAC-deficient child the worst candidate for it; mitotic slippage is the failure mode (PMID 30601084)

anti_directions.name: spindle poisons in a SAC-deficient background
anti_directions.agents: vinca alkaloids and taxanes - standard rhabdomyosarcoma chemotherapy
anti_directions.why: spindle poisons rely on a working checkpoint to arrest cells; MVA1 cells have a weakened checkpoint (PMID 20516114) and slip through mitosis (PMID 30601084). Flagged for the treating team as a hypothesis to weigh, never as advice to withhold standard therapy

evidence_ladder.purpose: every candidate drug is placed on one rung before it is argued; rung 1 is named, never submitted

rungs.label: approved for a related indication, with paediatric use
rungs.test: an approved drug with an openFDA label carrying a pediatric_use section or a ClinicalTrials.gov study in the tumour context that admits children

rungs.label: clinical trial in a related indication
rungs.test: a registered study of the drug in the disease or the tumour context

rungs.label: in-vivo model of aneuploidy or checkpoint deficiency
rungs.test: a cited animal result on the direction's mechanism (a PMID in evidence.tsv)

rungs.label: cell model in aneuploid or checkpoint-deficient cells
rungs.test: a cited cellular result on the direction's mechanism (a PMID in evidence.tsv)

rungs.label: mechanism only
rungs.test: the drug acts on a target in the direction's set and nothing above applies

evidence_ladder.rule: the rung is the highest test the drug passes; automated tests (approval, label, trials) and curated tests (a PMID read by a person) are printed side by side and never merged silently; a curated row may carry proxy=true when the cited result is for a same-axis compound rather than the approved molecule itself; the automated rungs 4 and 5 rest on a trial in the tumour context and therefore apply only to a direction marked context=true (the tumour-context direction) - a rhabdomyosarcoma trial says nothing about a checkpoint or proteostasis mechanism (refinement recorded in methodology 113 after the first grading run)

columns.name: role
columns.description: 'seed' when the mechanism card named this gene itself, 'pathway' when the Reactome expansion added it as a member of a matching pathway

columns.name: direction_ids

columns.name: uniprot

catalog.method: Seed targets are the union of the card's per-direction seed_targets, in card order. Pathway targets are every human ReferenceGeneProduct participating in a Reactome pathway that (a) contains the card's UniProt accession, per /data/mapping/UniProt/{acc}/pathways?species=9606, and (b) whose displayName matches /checkpoint|kinetochore|mitotic/i. A gene that is already a seed keeps role 'seed'. The pattern is a parameter of the expansion, not a constant: a different mechanism card passes its own.

columns.name: max_phase

columns.name: approved

columns.name: fda_label
columns.description: the openFDA label id, when one was found. **Empty means not checked** — only approved drugs were queried — which is not the same as 'no label exists'

columns.name: first_approval
columns.description: the year the drug was first approved, per ChEMBL

columns.name: atc
columns.description: ATC codes — the WHO's therapeutic classification of the drug, e.g. L01 for antineoplastics; useful for grouping candidates by what they are normally for

catalog.method: For every target in targets.tsv: Open Targets drugAndClinicalCandidates (a search for the exact approved symbol, then the target), ChEMBL mechanisms for every human target whose components declare that gene symbol, and one batched DGIdb interactions query over the whole symbol list. Rows are deduped on (drug_name.lower(), target_symbol); a row merged from several sources lists all of them in `source`. max_phase, first_approval and atc are then filled from one batched ChEMBL molecule lookup over every ChEMBL id any source produced, which also replaces a bare ChEMBL id with the preferred name. `approved` is the disjunction of ChEMBL max_phase == 4, an Open Targets clinical stage of APPROVAL, and DGIdb's own approved flag. openFDA is then queried once per approved drug name; `fda_label` is empty for a row that was never checked, which is not the same statement as false.

catalog.method: Two query families, both derived from the card: one cond= query for the card's disease name with any parenthetical gloss stripped, and one intr=<drug> cond=<tumour context> query per approved candidate drug name. The disease query walks up to 3 pages of 100; the per-drug queries take the first page only. A study matching two queries appears once per query, tagged in the `query` column. Every query and its hit count, including the zeros, is listed in snapshot.json.

catalog.method: Four query families over PubMed E-utilities: <gene> AND (repurposing OR inhibitor OR <anchor>); <pathway head phrase> AND drug; per direction, the direction name with its slash-separated segments OR'd, AND <anchor>; and the PMIDs the card itself cites. <anchor> is the last alphabetic word of the card's disease name. The direction family is the weak one: a long descriptive name becomes a long AND-chain and can match nothing. Those zeros are recorded in snapshot.json rather than papered over with a looser query.

evidence.claim: Chloroquine preferentially inhibited proliferation of trisomic mouse embryonic fibroblasts and aneuploid human cells in the Amon laboratory screen for aneuploidy-selective compounds.
Same screen result as chloroquine; hydroxychloroquine is the analogue used in paediatric rheumatology and was not itself tested.
AICAR, an AMPK activator, was aneuploidy-selective in trisomic and aneuploid cells; metformin is the market-approved AMPK-activating drug and was not itself tested.

Human aneuploid cell models mitigate proteotoxic stress by increasing protein degradation and are more sensitive to proteasome inhibition; aneuploidy level tracked the response of myeloma patients to proteasome inhibitors.

Induced chromosome missegregation in tubal epithelial cells caused misfolded-protein accumulation and enhanced vulnerability to proteasome inhibition; PTEN loss resensitised spheroids to proteasome inhibition in vitro and in vivo.

The NAD+ precursor nicotinamide mononucleotide raised BubR1 abundance in vivo, and SIRT2 overexpression extended median lifespan of BubR1 hypomorphic mice; niacin is the market-approved NAD+ precursor and was not itself tested.
Same in-vivo result; nicotinamide is the vitamin-form NAD+ precursor and was not itself tested.

HDAC2 and HDAC3 bind acetylated BubR1 in mitosis and drive its polyubiquitination and degradation, disassembling the mitotic checkpoint complex; no HDAC inhibitor drug was tested on BubR1 levels, so the drug row is inferred from the class mechanism.
BubR1 acetylation at lysine 250 by PCAF protects it from ubiquitin-dependent degradation and is required for checkpoint function; an acetylation-mimetic BubR1 is stabilised.
Same class-level mechanism as valproic acid (pan-HDAC inhibition); no vorinostat result on BubR1 levels is cited.
Lovastatin significantly reduced rhabdomyosarcoma cell proliferation; genetic inhibition of cholesterol biosynthesis halted xenograft growth - the in-vivo result is genetic, not pharmacological.
Same class result as lovastatin (HMGCR inhibition); simvastatin was not itself tested.
Same class result as lovastatin (HMGCR inhibition); atorvastatin was not itself tested, and carries a paediatric label indication (familial hypercholesterolaemia).

ALT is matched by list membership — variants_raw keeps a multi-allelic site comma-packed (G -> A,C in one row) while the annotations are one row per ALT, so the join tests that the annotated allele is an element of the split list rather than a substring of the packed string, which would match A against AT. register.statement: The disease mechanism in this proband is hypomorphic loss of BUB1B function: one null allele (stop_gained, exon 17 of 23) plus one partly functional allele (kinase-domain missense), leaving reduced BubR1 and a leaky spindle assembly checkpoint; there is no gain-of-function or dominant-negative component.
register.prediction: Public sources agree with the shape: ClinVar and the literature classify BUB1B MVA1 as autosomal recessive loss of function; every reported MVA1 genotype combines a null with a hypomorph or two hypomorphs; no BUB1B variant is annotated dominant or gain-of-function in ClinVar/OMIM; Reactome places BUB1B in the mitotic spindle checkpoint pathway.
register.refuted_by: Any ClinVar or OMIM record of a dominant or gain-of-function BUB1B mechanism, functional evidence that kinase-domain missense alleles act as dominant negatives, or the oracle returning no match for the BUB1B pair (which would make the mechanism argument moot).

register.statement: No market-approved drug acts directly on BubR1; approved candidates for this case will come only from pathway neighbours (spindle assembly checkpoint members) and from aneuploidy-stress, proteostasis or tumour-context directions.
register.prediction: Open Targets knownDrugs for BUB1B, ChEMBL mechanisms for human BUB1B targets and DGIdb interactions for BUB1B return zero molecules with max_phase 4 (approved); approved molecules appear only for other targets in the expanded set (for example AURKB, KIF11, PLK1, TTK, HDAC1-3, HSP90AA1, MTOR, PRKAA1).
register.refuted_by: Any molecule with an approved status (ChEMBL max_phase 4 or an FDA label) whose recorded mechanism of action names BUB1B/BubR1 as the target.

register.statement: Direction D1 (checkpoint reinforcement) yields no submittable drug: no market-approved molecule strengthens the spindle assembly checkpoint or reduces chromosome missegregation in checkpoint-deficient cells, so every approved D1 candidate the sources return is a checkpoint inhibitor or a spindle poison and D1 becomes the do-not table.
register.prediction: Among approved candidates attached to D1 seed targets in the refreshed snapshot, every action type is inhibitor, antagonist or tubulin-binding; no approved molecule reaches rung 2 or higher for a checkpoint-reinforcing result in evidence.tsv; the anti-direction table holds at least one D1 drug class.
register.refuted_by: An approved molecule with a cited cellular or animal result (a PMID) showing strengthened checkpoint signalling or reduced missegregation in SAC-deficient or aneuploid cells, placing it at rung 2 or higher under D1.

register.statement: Direction D2 (aneuploidy-selective stress) holds at least one market-approved compound with a cited result in aneuploid or checkpoint-deficient cell models, i.e. rung 2 or higher, and that evidence is for the approved molecule itself rather than only for an unapproved tool compound.
register.prediction: At least one approved drug acting on a D2 target (autophagy, proteasome, AMPK/energy stress, HSP90 or mTOR axis) carries a curated evidence row at rung 2 or higher with proxy=false; chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine is expected to be one from the Tang 2011 screen.
register.refuted_by: Every D2 evidence row at rung 2 or higher names an unapproved compound (AICAR, 17-AAG) with proxy=true, or no D2 row reaches rung 2 at all.

register.statement: Direction D3 (BubR1 stabilisation for a hypomorph) has an approved-drug route: a market-approved agent acts on a BubR1-stabilising axis (SIRT2/NAD+ or acetylation) and the axis carries in-vivo evidence of raised BubR1 in a BubR1-insufficient model, i.e. rung 3, possibly through a same-axis proxy compound.
register.prediction: evidence.tsv holds a rung-3 row for the NAD+ repletion axis citing PMID 24825348 (nicotinamide mononucleotide raised BubR1 in vivo in BubR1 hypomorphic mice), and the snapshot returns at least one approved NAD+ precursor or SIRT2-axis molecule (niacin/nicotinamide class) attached to a D3 target.
register.refuted_by: No approved molecule attaches to any D3 target in the snapshot, or the in-vivo BubR1 result cannot be tied to any approved molecule even as a same-axis proxy, leaving D3 at rung 1 or 2 only.

register.statement: Direction D4 (the child's tumour context, rhabdomyosarcoma) holds at least one approved, non-cytotoxic agent with a cited mechanistic result in rhabdomyosarcoma models (rung 2 or higher) and with paediatric safety data.
register.prediction: A statin (HMGCR) reaches rung 2 or higher from PMID 41249736 and carries an openFDA label with a pediatric_use section or a paediatric ClinicalTrials.gov study; the cytotoxic backbone drugs (vincristine, doxorubicin) also appear but are excluded as repurposing candidates because they are the standard of care, not a repurposing.
register.refuted_by: Every D4 approved candidate with rung 2 or higher is a cytotoxic already in the rhabdomyosarcoma standard of care, or the non-cytotoxic candidates have no paediatric label section and no paediatric trial.

register.statement: The automated stages of the repurposing pipeline are not specific to the mechanism: with the clinical side held fixed and the gene swapped for a decoy (NTRK3, the seeded pick from the step-2 decoy set; XDH, an unrelated metabolic enzyme), at least one of the four directions' approved drug sets overlaps a decoy card's approved set at Jaccard 0.10 or more, so the curated rung, not the automated stage, is what separates candidates.
register.prediction: D4 (TP53, MTOR, CDK4/6, IGF1R - broadly drugged cancer targets) overlaps at least one decoy's approved drug set at Jaccard >= 0.10; the decoy cards' automated rung distributions (approval, label, rhabdomyosarcoma trials) look like BUB1B's because the tumour-context queries are gene-independent.
register.refuted_by: Every direction's approved drug set has Jaccard < 0.10 against both decoy cards' approved sets - the automated pipeline alone already separates the mechanism from the decoys.

register.statement: Every drug shortlisted at rung 2 or higher for the BUB1B card has paediatric data: an openFDA label with a pediatric_use section, or a ClinicalTrials.gov study that admits children, in any indication.
register.prediction: For each shortlisted drug, pediatric_trials.tsv holds at least one study with a child age group or the label check records pediatric_use=true.
register.refuted_by: Any shortlisted drug at rung 2 or higher with neither a pediatric_use label section nor a ClinicalTrials.gov study admitting children.

register.statement: No chromosome in the sequenced sample -- autosome or X -- carries a mosaic aneuploidy at a cell fraction above its own measured detection limit.
register.prediction: Every chromosome's fold-over B-deviation sits inside the fitted beta-binomial null band, and every k-mer dosage interval covers the diploid expectation; each chromosome's result is quoted together with the smallest cell fraction its own data could have detected at 80 percent power.
register.refuted_by: One chromosome exceeds its own detection limit on either route -- reported with the estimated cell fraction, its interval, and the winning MAD-seq model; entry 037's flat karyogram is then superseded by a positive finding rather than by a power statement.

register.statement: The detection limit of the fold-over B-deviation test is at most 10 percent cell fraction for every autosome at this sample's heterozygous-site count and depth.
register.prediction: The simulated smallest detectable fraction at 80 percent power is no greater than 0.10 for each of the 22 autosomes.
register.refuted_by: Any autosome whose limit exceeds 0.10 -- that chromosome is named as a blind spot and no absence claim is made for it.

register.statement: Fold-over B-deviation detects a mosaic gain at a materially lower cell fraction than the mean B-allele-fraction statistic entry 037 used, on identical simulated sites.
register.prediction: Run through the same mixing harness on the same heterozygous-site histograms, the fold-over statistic's 80-percent-power fraction is at least 1 percentage point below the mean-BAF statistic's on a majority of autosomes.
register.refuted_by: The two limits agree within 1 percentage point on most autosomes -- entry 037 was not underpowered, and the re-test's contribution is confirmation rather than correction.

register.statement: The k-mer dosage route and the VCF allele-balance route agree on every chromosome within their stated intervals.
register.prediction: For each chromosome, the dosage bootstrap interval and the allele-balance fraction estimate interval overlap, or both are consistent with no event.
register.refuted_by: A chromosome where the two intervals do not overlap -- the step then names which instrument is wrong and why, rather than averaging them.

register.statement: The leave-one-chromosome-out baseline is stable: no chromosome's exclusion moves the genome-wide baseline beyond its bootstrap interval.
register.prediction: Recomputing the median of per-chromosome estimates with each chromosome held out in turn leaves every baseline inside the interval computed from the full set.
register.refuted_by: One chromosome's exclusion shifts the baseline beyond the interval -- the variegated failure mode Kong 2018 warned about is live in this sample, and every median-normalised route is flagged as such.

register.statement: The mixing simulation recovers two and three simultaneously affected chromosomes at 10 and 20 percent cell fraction, and does not flag the unaffected ones.
register.prediction: In each multi-chromosome design, every injected chromosome is detected at 80 percent power or better, and the false-positive rate among the unaffected chromosomes stays at or below the nominal 5 percent.
register.refuted_by: A design where recovery falls below 80 percent power, or where unaffected chromosomes are flagged above the nominal rate -- reported as the bound's blind spot for exactly the multi-chromosome case the disease name describes.

register.statement: Mitotic and meiotic trisomy are not separable at delta-BIC of 10 or more from arm-stratified allele-fraction band structure at cell fractions up to 20 percent, at this sample's depth and heterozygous-site counts.
register.prediction: On simulated meiotic and mitotic trisomies injected at 5, 10 and 20 percent, the five-model comparison assigns the correct mechanism with delta-BIC of 10 or more in fewer than half the replicates; the mechanism is therefore reported as not identifiable rather than called.
register.refuted_by: The comparison separates the two mechanisms at delta-BIC of 10 or more in a majority of replicates -- the mechanism call is then a real measurement and is handed to step 7's Track 2 card.

register.statement: The evidence ladder is independent of the measured aneuploid fraction: revising the mechanism card to version 4 with step 8's result (no autosome above its 2-3 % detection limit in the sequenced sample) changes no rung, no shortlist row and no do-not row; F8 acts only on how direction D2 is argued in the report, not on what it contains.
register.prediction: Re-running tools/track2_enrich.py --skip-live on card v4 reproduces evidence_ladder.tsv, shortlist.tsv and do_not.tsv byte-identical to the card-v3 run (same sha256 for all three), while every manifest names card version 4.
register.refuted_by: Any row of evidence_ladder.tsv, shortlist.tsv or do_not.tsv differs between the card-v3 and the card-v4 run - a rung, a flag, a verdict or a rank moved without any input table changing.

strategy.detail: Iteration 2, step 7: every approved drug on every direction placed on a rung (5 approved + paediatric, 4 trial in context, 3 in vivo, 2 cell model, 1 mechanism only) with the automated and the curated test printed side by side; one pre-registered claim per direction (H045-H048), one for the decoy control (H049), one for paediatric data (H050). tools/track2_enrich.py; entries 110-113.

strategy.title: Report structured along methods-form Q14
strategy.detail: Loss- versus gain-of-function, the pathway, the downstream consequence, and the drug x mechanism evidence table with a pathway diagram from the allele to each intervention point.

strategy.title: Verdicts: the pair is confirmed, the claims are settled
strategy.detail: The oracle's reply to submission 1 (083) confirmed the trans pair, so the mechanism card moved to version 3 (measured facts F1-F9 from iteration 2) and the Track 2 claims carry committed verdicts. The aneuploidy burden in the sample (F8) is the one fact still marked unmeasured: step 8 has not run.

strategy.title: One Track 2 submission, from the merged record
strategy.detail: Each oracle reply revises the card (a new version and a history entry, never an edit) and the snapshot is re-run. The final suggestion is produced once, after the last reply: all iterations' evidence merged, the ranking re-run on the confirmed pair, the report written from that merged state.
